entries.label: Brain-Machine Interface
key_players: MIT Laboratory for Human and Machine Haptics
entries.quote: HBMIs will allow human brains to control artificial devices designed to restore lost sensory and motor functions.
entries.note: No availability field. Timing in body text: "in the long run".

entries.label: Flexible Transistors
entries.quote: A compromise: transistors made from materials that combine the charge-shuttling power and speed of inorganics with the affordability and flexibility of organics.
entries.note: No availability field. Timing in body text: "within five years".

entries.label: Data Mining
entries.quote: Data mining didn't exist as a field until he helped pioneer it.
entries.note: No availability field and no timing in body text.

entries.label: Digital Rights Management
entries.quote: DRM will allow content owners to get much wider and deeper distribution than ever before.
entries.note: No availability field. Timing in body text: "a year or so away from seeing broad adoption".

entries.label: Biometrics
entries.quote: Personal digital assistants (PDAs) and cell phones are becoming our portal to the world, our transaction devices, our ID and maybe one day our passport.
entries.note: No availability field. Timing in body text: "two to three years".

entries.label: Natural Language Processing
entries.quote: HAL's modern-day counterparts are catching up fast.
entries.note: No availability field and no timing in body text.

entries.label: Microphotonics
entries.quote: Photonic crystals are to photons what semiconductors are to electrons, offering an excellent medium for controlling the flow of light.
entries.note: No availability field. Timing in body text: "five to 10 years".

entries.label: Untangling Code
entries.quote: Aspects allow programmers to write, view and edit a crosscutting concern as a separate entity.
entries.note: No availability field. Timing in body text: "by June" (AspectJ 1.0 release).

entries.label: Robot Design
entries.quote: To use robots to build robots.
entries.note: No availability field. Timing in body text: "five to 10 years".

entries.label: Microfluidics
entries.quote: Mass-produced, disposable microfluidic chips that make possible everything from drug discovery on a massive scale to at-home tests for common infections.
entries.note: No availability field. Timing in body text: "end of this year or early 2002".

notes: First edition, Technology Review Jan/Feb 2001 issue (web page dates it 2001-02-01). Ten entries. No edition-level availability field; timings noted per entry come from body text, read through a summarising fetch, so quotes and timings are medium confidence. Person names in the key-player lists were dropped (organizations only).
